# Statistics fundamentals and resources

## Why This Matters

Statistics helps you distinguish biological signal from noise and make defensible conclusions.

## Learning Outcomes

- Explain probability distributions and sampling variability.
- Perform and interpret hypothesis tests and confidence intervals.
- Understand linear models and regression assumptions.
- Select a suitable statistical method for common omics analyses.

## Suggested Time

- **Minimum**: 2 weeks (core concepts)
- **Recommended**: 3-4 weeks (with practice datasets)

## Key Concepts

- Probability Theory: Distributions, random variables
- Statistical Inference: Hypothesis testing, confidence intervals
- Regression Analysis: Linear and non-linear models
- Multivariate Statistics
- Multiple Testing and False Discovery Rate

## Recommended Resources

- **Books**:
  - *The Elements of Statistical Learning* by Trevor Hastie et al.
  - *Applied Multivariate Statistical Analysis* by Richard A. Johnson
  - *Statistical Inference* by George Casella and Roger L. Berger

- **Online Courses**:
  - [Statistics and Data Science](https://www.edx.org/professional-certificate/mitx-statistics-and-data-science) on edX
  - [Probability and Statistics](https://www.coursera.org/learn/probability-intro) on Coursera

## Mini Project

- Download a small gene-expression dataset.
- Run basic quality checks and summary plots.
- Compare two groups with an appropriate test.
- Write 5-8 lines explaining assumptions and limitations.
